q: Which study design is commonly used to estimate point prevalence?
why: Cross-sectional designs can estimate prevalence with suitable sampling and case definitions.

q: A study selects participants based on outcome status and then assesses prior exposure. This is:
why: Case-control studies sample cases and controls by outcome status.

options: To reduce selective outcome switching and clarify the analysis
why: Pre-specification improves transparency and supports design and analysis planning.

q: Which is an example of a surrogate endpoint?
options: A biomarker used instead of a direct clinical outcome
why: A surrogate substitutes for a direct outcome and may not predict patient benefit.

options: Improves reporting transparency but does not guarantee sound methods
why: Reporting quality and methodological quality are related but not identical.
